key_insight: Orthogonalized updates paired with gradient-norm-based adaptive stepsizes improve primal–dual coordination in nonconvex–strongly-concave minimax optimization without problem-dependent tuning.
engineering_relevance: The framework targets unstable, stepsize-sensitive minimax training by automatically balancing coupled primal and dual updates.
method: Orthogonalize update directions to reduce update anisotropy.
Use accumulated gradient norms to adapt AdaSGDA stepsizes, achieving an O(T^−1/4) convergence rate.
Add variance reduction in AdaSGDA-VR to achieve an O(T^−1/3) rate.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical convergence guarantees and extensive experiments showing competitive performance, but does not specify benchmarks or numerical gains.
watch_item: The guarantees assume nonconvex–strongly-concave objectives; orthogonalization and variance reduction may also add implementation overhead.
paper_title: Orthogonal Updates for the Win: Towards Accelerated Adaptive Minimax Optimization
